builds.howItPlays: You put cheap units on the board early and empower them, which also empowers Ambessa, so she can spend a rune to ready one of your units and send it into another fight. Kennen, Keeper of Balance can be hidden face down for a rune, then played for free on your opponent's turn to stun a defender for 2 more, and Hidden Blade kills a unit at a battlefield, though its owner draws 2 cards.
builds.whyYou: You like having units on the board from the first turns, but you care more about winning the fight that matters than about racing. You enjoy keeping a card face down and a unit in hand that can jump into a fight at the last moment, so your opponent can't be sure how big a combat will get. You're fine with a game that runs into the middle turns, because every fight you win on a battlefield brings you closer to holding it. If sizing up each combat and picking the moment to strike sounds fun, this Ambessa suits you.
builds.ratingNotes: 2026-09-25 re-rate: relabelled Aggro to Midrange, and coordinates moved from 7.5/8/5.5/5.5 to 6/6/6.5/4 (pace -1.5, stance -2, complexity +1, variance -1.5). The old numbers came from two guide articles with no deck behind them, and deckListUrl pointed at the bare /decks page. The new Build is the picked Kennen Stun Ambessa style, scored from three decks under the current rubric. Scored decks (pace/stance/complexity/variance): https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/7358ba07-c17c-4349-a545-f2a44f71212b Katchouze AMBESSA_UPDATED, edited 2026-09-23 after the ban, 6/6/7/3.5, judged Tempo (16 reactive cards); https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/f4a97c37-850a-4ad5-bf45-6f619185a9f0 Best of Singapore RQ, CBL Dags, 6.5/6.5/6.5/4.5, Midrange (the scorer suggested Aggro, but the list leans on Rampage, Hidden Blade and reactions rather than racing); https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/0f7ce5f8-e5e1-46ea-9124-8a818f664b80 SargonVito Ambessa Midrange, 6/6/6.5/4, Midrange (the scorer suggested Tempo on 14 reactive cards; the plan is empowered board presence). Mean: Midrange 6/6/6.5/4, labels Tempo, Midrange, Midrange (tools.ts style). Adjustments: complexity +1 on every sheet, because the Legend empowers itself off every other empower and spends that to ready a unit, a choice to time every turn. What decided each Axis: pace comes from 8 or 9 cheap units per 40 (Pit Rookie, Legion Marauder, Irresistible Faefolk), held back by 3 to 5 cards costing 5+ (Vi, Peacekeeper, Rengar, Ambessa, Respected and Feared). Stance comes from 22 to 25 pressure against 11 to 13 answers (Hidden Blade, Rampage, Public Execution, Sabotage, Tactical Retreat, Repulse), with 12 to 16 reactive cards pulling it toward the middle. Complexity comes from setup on empower units (Kayle, Justified, Legion Marauder, Guttural Roar), reaction-speed Kennen, Nidalee and Vi, and the Legend. Variance is low: there are no luck or swing cards, 6 to 8 removal and mostly 3-ofs. No Axis showed a 2+ gap between formula and judgment. Legend: 'When you empower something else, empower me. Disempower me, [Rune], [Tap]: Ready a unit.'
